chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He said: 'The walking of a man to attend to the need of his believing brother is recorded for him as ten good deeds, and ten bad deeds are erased from him, and ten ranks are elevated for him.' He said: 'And I do not know him except that he said: And it is equivalent to freeing ten necks, and is superior to performing Itikaf for a month in the Sacred Mosque.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for helping a Muslim brother in need according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize the social dimension of worship, where practical assistance to a believer is elevated to the status of major acts of devotion. The comparison to freeing ten slaves and surpassing a month of Itikaf in the Sacred Mosque underscores the high value Shia scholarship places on active solidarity (ta'awun) over isolated ritualism. This highlights the principle that relieving a fellow Muslim's distress is a direct means of spiritual purification and elevation in the hereafter.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muhammad Bin Marwan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘The walking of the man regarding a need of his Momin brother would have ten good deeds Written for him, and ten sins Deleted from him, and ten levels would be Elevated for him’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I do not know it except that heasws said: ‘And it equates to (freeing) ten necks, and superior than performing Itikaaf for a month in the Sacred Masjid’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Muhammad ibn Marwan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘For a believer’s walking to help a believing brother (in belief) ten good deeds are written for him, ten of his sins are deleted and he is raised ten degrees in meritorious status.’ The narrator has said, ‘I do not know what else the Imam said, but (I do know) he (the Imam) said, ‘It is equal to setting ten slaves free and performing ‘I’tikaf (a certain form of worship) in the Sacred Mosque.’”
